schema_note: PIN-P1 (f.4): array of pinned-k entries. The single-k v0 file (k=18 only) is preserved at entries[0]; new k values land via append.

entries.format: snarkjs ptau (sections 1-7; we consume sections 1-3 only)
entries.source_mirror: PSE (Privacy & Scaling Explorations) AWS S3, eu-central-1
notes: Anyone can re-derive the sha256 via verification_command above.
The .ptau format is SnarkJS-style binary with 7 sections; we consume sections 1 (header), 2 (tauG1), and 3 (tauG2) only.
Trust model: 1-of-N — one honest contributor among 86 suffices for the SRS to be cryptographically safe.

entries.source_mirror: PSE (Privacy & Scaling Explorations) AWS S3, eu-central-1
entries.consumes: PIN-P1 (f.3) leaf circuit candidate (k_leaf ~21–22 depending on partition cost)
notes: PIN-P1 (f.4) allocation — hash unpinned until an operator fetches the file, captures sha256, and lands a follow-up PR per the WP-M1b.2 stability rule (srs.rs header).
load_srs(22, _) returns SrsLoadError::HashNotPinned with this URL until the hash lands here + in srs::PINNED.

entries.source_mirror: PSE (Privacy & Scaling Explorations) AWS S3, eu-central-1
entries.consumes: PIN-P1 (f.3) root circuit candidate (k_root ~22–24 depending on accumulator per-leaf row cost)
notes: PIN-P1 (f.4) allocation — hash unpinned until an operator fetches the file. Same gating semantics as k=22.

entries.source_mirror: PSE (Privacy & Scaling Explorations) AWS S3, eu-central-1

notes: PIN-P1 (f.4) allocation — hash unpinned until an operator fetches the file. f.4 spec calls for k=25 as the recommended pin (handoffs/PIN_DGX_NEXT_STEPS.md §(f.4)).
